solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Development angle initially ignored in training

indicators.note: ignored says that letter is left out of the training word

parts.note: training is education

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word angle

explanation.surface: A teacher's slant is dropped from a course of instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes A from 'angle'; 'ignored' drops that A from EDUCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Eduction is a rare word for the act of drawing out or bringing forth, hence a development.

clue.text: Ballet star has no regrets coming up short

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue says the letters are read from the bottom upwards
short says the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: having no regrets is regretting nothing: RUES (regrets) plus NADA (nothing)

explanation.surface: A lead dancer feels no remorse after a career cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims RUESNADA to RUESNAD; 'coming up' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseur is a male ballet dancer, the French word for a dancer, so a ballet star.

clue.text: Left cutting remark in personal manner

indicators.note: cutting says the left word slices into the middle of the remark word

parts.note: a remark is a comment
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A departing person's sharp remark about someone's personal manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left cutting remark' reads like a barbed comment; 'cutting' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Comportment means how a person carries and conducts themselves, their bearing or demeanour.

clue.text: Dramatist elevated in Verlaine's biography

indicators.note: elevated says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A playwright features prominently in a life of the French poet Verlaine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'elevated' means read upwards: the hidden NESBI turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: River's northern one a gelatinous substance blocks

definitions.note: read as 'River is', the definition followed by a link

indicators.note: blocks says the jelly sits between the one and the a, obstructing them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
agar is a jelly made from seaweed

explanation.surface: A river's northern reach is choked by some jelly-like matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niagara is the North American river famous for its falls on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: God as revealed in performance by Salvationists

parts.note: SA stands for the Salvation Army, whose members are Salvationists
a turn is a performer's act in a show

explanation.surface: A deity appears in a show put on by the Salvation Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn was the Roman god of agriculture and time, identified with the Greek Cronus.

clue.text: Timepiece best in sample collection

indicators.note: in says the best word goes inside the sample word

parts.note: a swatch is a set of fabric samples
top means best

explanation.surface: A watch rated finest among a range of samples.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Swatch the watchmaker, which helps sell 'Timepiece'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopwatch is a timepiece that can be started and stopped to time events precisely.

clue.text: Company that sends up anything

indicators.note: sends up in a down clue says the letters are read upwards

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything

explanation.surface: A firm that mocks anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends up' looks like mockery but signals a reversal; OWT is Yorkshire dialect for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'two's company, three's a crowd' makes a pair of people company.

clue.text: Fox on road around some turning

indicators.note: around says the on-and-road pair wraps the turned word

parts.note: re means on or about

indicators.note: turning says the word for some is read backwards

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A fox out on a road, circling at some bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' turns the word for some round, and 'around' has the on-plus-road pair wrap it; 'on' as RE is the sense 'regarding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reynard is the traditional name for the fox in medieval fables.

clue.text: Collecting bits and pieces?

parts.note: bits and pieces are coins, as in a threepenny bit or a fifty-pence piece, so collecting them is coin study

explanation.surface: Hoarding odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the study and collection of coins and medals, the formal name for coin collecting.

clue.text: Grieve for bird that disappeared inside mountain

indicators.note: inside says the bird goes within the mountain word

parts.note: ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis
the moa was a flightless New Zealand bird, now extinct

explanation.surface: Mourning a bird lost somewhere on a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan something is to lament or express sorrow over it.

clue.text: First man to hold pen maybe creating massive barrier

indicators.note: to hold says the first man's name surrounds the swan word

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: The first man picks up a pen and builds an enormous wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is not a writing tool here but a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aswan Dam on the Nile in Egypt is a huge embankment holding back Lake Nasser.

clue.text: Eats nuts in Homer, which is anomalous

definitions.note: eats as a noun, informal for food

indicators.note: anomalous means irregular, so the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone eats nuts in the Odyssey, which is out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eats' looks like a verb but is the noun, food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is slang for food, and nourishment is food that sustains the body.

clue.text: Opposing or supporting check by social worker

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a test is a check
an ant is a worker in an insect colony, a social insect

explanation.surface: Arguing for or against an inspection by a social services employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is an insect, not a carer.
explanation.definitionFit: Protestant in its root sense is an adjective meaning protesting, objecting against something.

clue.text: Sleepy old man dropping article in strait

indicators.note: in says the shortened old man goes inside the strait

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England

indicators.note: dropping says the article is let fall from the word man

parts.note: taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A drowsy old man loses an item while crossing a strait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes the article from 'man', and 'in' puts the result inside the strait; the Solent lies off the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent is a formal synonym for drowsy, inclined to sleep.

clue.text: Tongue in ancient city to be enough for listeners

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: for listeners says a word is to be taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: do means suffice, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: A language in an old city is adequate for those listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means language, and Urdu is spoken in Pakistan and India.

clue.text: Affected material finally cut

indicators.note: finally cut says the last letter of the material is trimmed off

parts.note: tweed is a woollen cloth

explanation.surface: A precious fabric is snipped at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively quaint or sentimental, hence affected in style.

clue.text: Metal bolt and stuff

parts.note: to wolf is to bolt food
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A metal bolt and other material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' is the eating verb, not the hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is another name for tungsten, a heavy metallic element.

clue.text: Spokesman opening with dramatic work

parts.note: a mouth is an opening
a piece is a play or composition

explanation.surface: A spokesperson starts proceedings with a theatrical production.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouthpiece is someone who speaks on behalf of another, a representative.

clue.text: Stressed and too drunk to go to bed?

definitions.text: too drunk to go to bed?
definitions.meaning: cryptically still up, not retired for the night, and tight, which is drunk

explanation.surface: Tense, and too drunk to make it to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense and nervy is the usual sense; the playful one splits it as awake and tipsy.

clue.text: Scottish historian in Cumbrian city to speak

indicators.note: to speak says the city's name is taken as pronounced

parts.note: Carlisle is the county town of Cumbria in north-west England

explanation.surface: A Scots historian gives a talk in a city in Cumbria.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlisle, a city in north-west England near the Scottish border, sounds the same as the historian's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle was the Scottish historian who wrote The French Revolution.

clue.text: One used to beat dispirited infantry

parts.note: flat means low in spirits
foot soldiers are the infantry

explanation.surface: Someone employed to thrash downhearted foot soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' is a police patrol round, not a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatfoot is slang for a police officer, who walks a beat.

clue.text: Hard men in secret place make drastic cuts

indicators.note: in says the hard-and-men letters go inside the secret place

parts.note: a den is a hidden retreat
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Tough men in a hideout carry out severe cutbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: removing horns is a literal drastic cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To dehorn cattle is to cut off their horns, a severe trimming.

clue.text: Capital at one time husband invested in food store

indicators.note: invested in says the husband is placed inside the store word

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen

explanation.surface: A husband once put money into a capital food shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi was the seat of the Mughal empire and later of British India; New Delhi is now India's capital.

clue.text: Mug collection regularly goes astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's collection of mugs keeps going missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' means face, as in a police mugshot, not a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogues' gallery is a police file of photographs of known criminals' faces.

clue.text: State purpose falling short

indicators.note: falling short says the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: a goal is a purpose or aim

explanation.surface: A government's aim fails to deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a small state on the west coast of India.

clue.text: Influence thing done by little devil

parts.note: an imp is a small demon or a mischievous child
an act is a deed, a thing done

explanation.surface: The effect of something carried out by a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact means a strong effect or influence on something.

clue.text: Cardinal in there crippled after tango

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters follow the tango letter

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: crippled means damaged, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A church cardinal in there, disabled after a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' means a cardinal number, not a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are counting numbers such as one, two and three, of which this is one.
